routes.label: Divide each polygon into central triangles

question: The apothem of a square having its area numerically equal to its perimeter is compared with the apothem of an equilateral triangle having its area numerically equal to its perimeter. The first apothem will be:
solution:
Both figures are regular polygons, so joining the center to every vertex divides each figure into triangles whose heights are its apothem. This connects the apothem directly to both area and perimeter.

Let \(a\) be the numerical length of the apothem, \(P>0\) the numerical perimeter, and \(K\) the numerical area, using a common length unit and its square unit. Adding the triangle areas gives
\[
K=\frac12a\,(\text{sum of the side lengths})
=\frac12aP.
\]
The condition \(K=P\) therefore yields
\[
P=\frac12aP,
\qquad a=2,
\]
where division by \(P\) is valid because the polygon is nondegenerate.

This applies to both the square and the equilateral triangle. Their apothems are equal, so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
